title: Three Sum
description:
Given an integer array nums, return all unique triplets [nums[i], nums[j], nums[k]] such that i != j, i != k, and j != k, and nums[i] + nums[j] + nums[k] == 0.

Notice that the solution set must not contain duplicate triplets. The order of the triplets and the order of elements inside a triplet does not matter.

Implement an algorithm that runs in O(n²) time and uses constant extra space (excluding the output).

examples.explanation: The distinct triplets that sum to zero are [-1, -1, 2] and [-1, 0, 1].
No three numbers sum to zero.
The only triplet is [0, 0, 0].

starter.python:
def threeSum(self, nums: List[int]) -> List[List[int]]:
    pass

hints: Sort the array to simplify the two-pointer search.
Fix one element and use two pointers for the remaining two elements to find the target sum.
Skip duplicate values for the fixed element and for the two pointers to avoid duplicate triplets.
solution: Sort the array. Iterate with index i from 0 to n-3. If nums[i] > 0, break because sum cannot be zero. If i > 0 and nums[i] == nums[i-1], skip to avoid duplicates. Use two pointers left = i+1 and right = n-1. While left < right, compute sum. If sum == 0, add triplet to result, then move left and right past duplicate values. If sum < 0, increment left. If sum > 0, decrement right. Return the result.
constraints: The solution set must not contain duplicate triplets.
Each element may be used only once per triplet.

title: Product of Array Except Self
description:
Given an integer array nums, return an array answer such that answer[i] is equal to the product of all the elements of nums except nums[i].

The product of any prefix or suffix is guaranteed to fit in a 32-bit integer. You must write an algorithm that runs in O(n) time and without using the division operation.

Solve the problem in O(1) extra space (the output array does not count as extra space).

examples.explanation: The only non-zero product appears when the zero is excluded.
Basic case with minimum length 2.

starter.python:
def productExceptSelf(self, nums: List[int]) -> List[int]:
    pass

hints: Compute the prefix product for each position (product of all elements to the left).
Store the prefix products in the output array initially.
Traverse from the right keeping a running suffix product and multiply it with the corresponding prefix product in the output array.
solution: Initialize result array of same length. Set result[0] = 1. For i from 1 to n-1, result[i] = result[i-1] * nums[i-1] (prefix product). Then initialize a suffix product variable = 1. For i from n-1 down to 0, multiply result[i] by suffix, then update suffix = suffix * nums[i]. Return result.
constraints: The product of all elements fits in a 32-bit integer.
The output array does not count as extra space.

title: Subarray Sum Equals K
description:
Given an array of integers nums and an integer k, return the total number of continuous subarrays whose sum equals to k.

The subarrays can consist of positive and negative numbers, and the same subarray must not be counted twice.

Your solution must run in O(n) time.

examples.explanation: The subarrays that sum to 2 are [1,1] (indices 0-1) and [1,1] (indices 1-2).
Subarrays [1,2] and [3] sum to 3.
Every subarray sums to 0. Total subarrays = 3*(3+1)/2 = 6.

hints: Use a running prefix sum and a hash map to store how many times a particular sum has been seen.
At each step, check if (current_prefix_sum - k) exists in the map; if so, add its frequency to the count.
Initialize the map with {0: 1} to account for subarrays that start from the beginning.
solution: Initialize a hash map with {0: 1} and a running sum variable count = 0, sum = 0. Iterate through the array. For each element, add to sum. If (sum - k) is in the map, add map[sum - k] to count. Then increment map[sum] by 1. Return count.
constraints: The answer fits in a 32-bit integer.

title: Find First and Last Position of Element in Sorted Array
description:
Given an array of integers nums sorted in non-decreasing order, find the starting and ending position of a given target value.

If the target is not found in the array, return [-1, -1]. You must write an algorithm with O(log n) runtime complexity.

The array may contain duplicates and the targets can be any integer within the given constraints.

examples.explanation: First occurrence of 8 is at index 3, last at index 4.
6 does not appear in the array.
Empty array always returns [-1,-1].

hints: Implement a binary search that finds the leftmost (first) occurrence of the target.
Implement another binary search that finds the rightmost (last) occurrence.
If the leftmost index is not within bounds or the element at that index is not the target, return [-1, -1].
solution: Use two separate binary searches. The first search looks for the first position where nums[mid] >= target, moving right when nums[mid] < target. The second search looks for the last position where nums[mid] <= target, moving left when nums[mid] > target. After finding both, verify that the left index is valid and nums[left] == target; otherwise return [-1, -1].
constraints: nums is sorted in non-decreasing order.

description:
You are given an n x n 2D matrix representing an image. Rotate the image by 90 degrees clockwise.

You must rotate the image in-place, which means you have to modify the input matrix directly. Do not allocate another 2D matrix for the rotation.

The rotation should be performed on the original matrix, and the result should be readable from the same variable after the function call.

Reverse each row of the transposed matrix.
Alternatively, rotate groups of four cells in place, but the transpose-reverse method is easier to implement.
solution: First, transpose the matrix: for i from 0 to n-1, for j from i+1 to n-1, swap matrix[i][j] and matrix[j][i]. Then, reverse each row: for each row, swap the first with the last, second with second last, etc. This achieves a 90-degree clockwise rotation in O(n²) time and O(1) extra space.

title: Merge Intervals
description:
Given an array of intervals where intervals[i] = [start_i, end_i], merge all overlapping intervals, and return an array of the non-overlapping intervals that cover all the intervals in the input.

The result should be returned as a new array, and the original input may be sorted or not. Two intervals overlap if the start of one is less than or equal to the end of the other.

Your solution must sort the intervals appropriately and merge them in a single pass.

examples.explanation: Intervals [1,3] and [2,6] overlap, so they are merged into [1,6].
Intervals [1,4] and [4,5] are considered overlapping and merged to [1,5].
After sorting, [0,4] and [1,4] merge into [0,4].

hints: Sort the intervals by their start time.
Iterate through the sorted intervals and compare each with the last interval in the result list.
If the current interval overlaps with the last one (current.start <= last.end), merge them by updating last.end = max(last.end, current.end). Otherwise, add it to the result.
solution: Sort intervals by start time. Initialize result list with the first interval. For each subsequent interval, check if it overlaps with the last interval in result (current.start <= last.end). If so, update last.end = max(last.end, current.end). Otherwise, add the current interval to result. Return the result list.
space_complexity: O(n) for output (or O(1) extra if sorting in-place)
constraints: The intervals are not necessarily sorted.

title: Next Permutation
description:
Implement the next permutation, which rearranges numbers into the lexicographically next greater permutation of numbers.

If such an arrangement is not possible, it must rearrange it as the lowest possible order (i.e., sorted in ascending order). The replacement must be in-place and use only constant extra memory.

The algorithm should run in O(n) time and modify the input array directly.

examples.explanation: The next permutation after 1-2-3 is 1-3-2.
3-2-1 is the last permutation, so it wraps around to the first.
1-1-5 → 1-5-1 is the next greater permutation.

starter.python:
def nextPermutation(self, nums: List[int]) -> None:
    """
    Do not return anything, modify nums in-place.
    """
    pass

hints: Traverse from the right to find the first element that is smaller than its next element (let's call it the pivot).
From the right, find the smallest element that is larger than the pivot and swap them.
Reverse the suffix starting just after the pivot's original position.
solution: Find the largest index i such that nums[i] < nums[i+1]. If no such i exists, reverse the whole array and return. Then find the largest index j > i such that nums[j] > nums[i]. Swap nums[i] and nums[j]. Finally, reverse the subarray from i+1 to the end. This yields the next lexicographical permutation in O(n) time and O(1) extra space.

title: Maximum Product Subarray
description:
Given an integer array nums, find a contiguous non-empty subarray that has the largest product, and return the product.

The subarray must contain at least one number. The product may be negative, and you must handle both positive and negative numbers efficiently.

Your solution should run in O(n) time and use constant extra space.

examples.explanation: The subarray [2,3] has the largest product 6.
The result cannot be 2 because [-2,-1] is not contiguous. The best is 0.
The whole array product -2 * 3 * -4 = 24 gives the maximum.

starter.python:
def maxProduct(self, nums: List[int]) -> int:
    pass

hints: Keep track of both the maximum and minimum product ending at the current position.
When the current number is negative, the maximum can become the minimum and vice versa, so swap them before multiplying.
Update the global maximum after each step.
solution: Initialize result = nums[0], current_max = nums[0], current_min = nums[0]. For i from 1 to n-1, if nums[i] < 0, swap current_max and current_min. Then current_max = max(nums[i], current_max * nums[i]), current_min = min(nums[i], current_min * nums[i]). Update result = max(result, current_max). Return result.
constraints: The product of any subarray fits in a 32-bit integer.

title: Find All Duplicates in an Array
description:
Given an integer array nums of length n where all the integers are in the range [1, n] and each integer appears at most twice, return an array of all the integers that appear twice.

You must implement an algorithm that runs in O(n) time and uses only constant extra space (excluding the output). You may assume the input array is mutable and can be modified.

examples.explanation: 2 and 3 appear twice.
1 appears twice.
No duplicates when length is 1.

hints: Use the fact that numbers are in the range [1, n] — each number can be mapped to an index (value - 1).
Mark the visited number by negating the value at its corresponding index.
If the number at that index is already negative, the current number is a duplicate.
solution: Iterate through the array. For each number x, use abs(x)-1 as index. If nums[index] < 0, we have seen this number before, so add abs(x) to result. Otherwise, negate nums[index] to mark it. After traversal, return the result list. This uses the input array for marking and achieves O(n) time and O(1) extra space.
constraints: Each element appears once or twice.
Do not use extra space besides the output list.

title: Contiguous Array
description:
Given a binary array nums, return the maximum length of a contiguous subarray with an equal number of 0 and 1.

The array consists only of 0s and 1s. The subarray may start and end anywhere, and the goal is to maximize its length.

Your solution should run in O(n) time and use O(n) auxiliary space.

examples.explanation: The whole array has one 0 and one 1.
Either [0,1] (indices 0-1) or [1,0] (indices 1-2) has equal number.
The subarray [0,1,1,0] (indices 0-3) has two 0s and two 1s.
